chunks: Amr ibn Uthman narrated from Ali ibn Abdullah al-Bajali from Khalid ibn Mad al-Qalanisi from Abu Abd al-Lah (peace be upon him) who said:
Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon them both) said: 'A tasbihah (supplication/remembrance) in Mecca is better than the khums of the two Iraqs, spent in the way of Allah.'
And he said: 'Whoever completes the Quran in Mecca will not die until he sees the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) and sees his dwelling place in Paradise.'

key_terms.الْعِرَاقَيْنِ: The two Iraqs, referring to the regions of Iraq (often Basra and Kufa or Eastern and Western Iraq) known for their wealth and agricultural produce.
key_terms.تَسْبِيحَةٌ: A specific form of dhikr or supplication, often referring to the phrases of glorification.
key_terms.خَتَمَ الْقُرْآنَ: To complete the Quran, typically by reciting it from beginning to end.
key_terms.خَرَاجِ: Land tax or tribute, here used metaphorically for the khums or significant wealth.
key_terms.مَنْزِلَهُ: His dwelling place or station in Paradise.
key_terms.يَرَى رَسُولَ اللَّهِ: To see the Prophet Muhammad, a high honor in the afterlife or during life.

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual reward of completing the Quran in Mecca according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In the context of *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, this hadith underscores the unique spiritual economy of Mecca, where acts of devotion like *tasbihah* yield rewards comparable to the substantial fiscal contribution of the *khums* of the two Iraqs. Furthermore, it links the completion of the Quran in this sacred space to the eschatological promise of *ru'ya* (vision) of the Prophet and his household, reflecting the Shia emphasis on the intercessory and visionary connection with the Ahl al-Bayt in the afterlife.
